quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — Case File: My Best Day
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Past Simple (Irregular Verbs: went, saw, felt, made, gave)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Storytelling with Irregular Verbs
content: Problem: Students often apply the regular "-ed" rule to irregular verbs.

Solution: This week anchors 5 high-frequency irregular verbs (went, saw, felt, made, gave) to a highly personal, emotional context: "My Best Day Ever." By connecting the irregular form to a vivid memory, students memorize the chunk rather than analyzing the rule.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the 5 irregular verbs through a recount of a beach trip. Focus on meaning and form recognition.
Session 2: Practice the verbs with sequence words (First, Then) to build narrative flow.
Session 3: Full production. Students write and present their own "Best Day" story using the target verbs without scaffolding.

methodology.title: 2.3 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Hand the student a base verb card (go). The student must physically step forward and say the past form (went) in a full sentence.
Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): Information Gap: The Mystery Trip. Student A has the morning events. Student B has the afternoon events. They ask questions to complete the itinerary.

content: Science: Why Things Float and Sink
Objects float when they are LESS DENSE than water. They sink when they are MORE DENSE than water!
• Density = how much 'stuff' is packed into a space  • Cork floats  • Iron sinks
• A steel ship FLOATS because it is shaped to trap air — air is very light!

listening_script.text: Last Sunday, Leo went to the beach with his friends. First, he saw a big ship on the water. Then, he made a large sandcastle. He felt very proud. Finally, his friend gave him a cool shell. It was a great trip.

teacher_contents.speaking_notes:
SPEAKING CHECKPOINT — Teacher Guidance (do NOT share with students):

Student A: Names one thing Max did at the beach on his best day (e.g., "Max went to the beach and made a sandcastle").
Student B: Adds what Max felt or what his mom gave (e.g., "His mom gave him a shell. He felt very happy").
Goal: Use went / made / felt / gave correctly — W35 irregular verbs in a personal story.

PULL-OUT TASK (S1):
— Show a beach picture. Ask: "What did Max do? What did his mom give him?"
— Scaffold weaker students: "Max WENT to ___. He MADE ___. He FELT ___."
— Target elicitation: went / made / felt / gave — confirm no 'maked', 'gived', or 'feeled'.

COMMUNICATIVE TASK TIP:
— Model immediately: "We say MADE (not 'maked'), GAVE (not 'gived'), FELT (not 'feeled')."
— Stronger students: chain all 5 verbs: "Max WENT to the beach. He SAW shells. He MADE a castle. His mom GAVE him a bag. He FELT proud."
